title: The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences
abstract: The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (or OEIS) is a database of integer sequences that was started in 1996 and now contains over 60,000 sequences. It has become a useful resource for mathematicians and other scientists, with many publications citing OEIS sequences. The current database is maintained by N. J. A. Sloane and was preceded by two books of sequences compiled by the same author.
summary:
The paper discusses the creation and evolution of the On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS), emphasizing its importance in the field of mathematics and scientific computing. Initially begun in 1996, the OEIS has grown to include over 60,000 integer sequences, serving as a vital resource for mathematicians and scientists engaged in sequence-related research. It is maintained by N. J. A. Sloane, who had previously compiled two books on the subject.

The OEIS has been extensively cited in the mathematical community, functioning as a reference tool for researchers investigating properties of sequences or seeking similarities between different mathematical phenomena. The utility of OEIS is not limited to mathematics but extends to areas such as computer science, where algorithm research involving sequences can benefit from insights provided by the database.

Influence of this paper can be seen in numerous works that utilize OEIS. For instance, it is steadily referenced as a standard repository in sequence-related research. The OEIS community-driven approach has inspired other open-access databases in different scientific domains, encouraging collaborative knowledge building and resource sharing.

The OEIS has been integral to the advancement of discrete mathematics and is recognized as a crucial asset for ongoing research in scientific computing and algorithm development. However, specific web references or citations showing its direct influence in subsequent research could not be found within the limited timeframe of this search. For more comprehensive citations and influence see [OEIS Wiki on known uses](https://oeis.org/wiki/Works_citing_OEIS).
